title: pubba sutta
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.
groupSub: The Nearest Cause for the Origination of dukkha

paras.en:
‘What now is vedanā?
What is the origin of vedanā?
What is the way leading to the origination of vedanā?
What is the cessation of vedanā?
What is the way leading to the cessation of vedanā?
What is the gratification in vedanā?
What is the danger?
What is the way out?’

Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me:
‘There are these three vedanā: pleasant vedanā,
painful vedanā, neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā.
This is called vedanā.
With the arising of contact there is the arising of vedanā. Craving is the way leading to the origination of vedanā. With the cessation of contact there is the cessation of vedanā.

This Noble Eightfold Path is the way leading to the cessation of vedanā; that is,
right view, right intention,
right speech, right action, right livelihood,
right effort, right awareness, right concentration.

The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on vedanā: this is the gratification in vedanā.
That vedanā is impermanent, dukkha,
and subject to change: this is the danger in vedanā.

The removal and abandonment of desire and craving
for vedanā: this is the way out of vedanā.’”
